title: Poached Rhubarb in Elderflower
subtitle: Sharp rhubarb baked in a light elderflower syrup until just tender
excerpt: Rhubarb batons roasted in a light elderflower and orange syrup in a low oven until just soft and holding their shape, served cold with the blush-pink poaching liquid spooned over.
sourceNotes: Rhubarb responds better to oven poaching than stovetop, the indirect heat is gentle enough to keep the batons intact, whereas simmering in a pan tends to produce mush. Elderflower is a classic British pairing with rhubarb; it lifts the sharpness without masking it.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead. Keeps well in the fridge in its syrup.

content.text: Poached rhubarb in elderflower is rhubarb cut into batons and roasted in a low oven with a light syrup of elderflower cordial, orange, and sugar until just tender but still holding its shape. The oven method is gentler than stovetop poaching and gives intact batons rather than collapsing threads. The syrup turns a vivid blush pink from the rhubarb's colour. Serve cold, with Greek yoghurt or whipped cream.

Preheat the oven to 160°C fan. Lay the rhubarb batons in a single layer in a baking dish, they should fit snugly but not be piled up. In a small bowl or jug, stir together the sugar, elderflower cordial, and orange juice until the sugar begins to dissolve. Pour over the rhubarb. Add the vanilla pod if using.

Cover the dish tightly with foil. Bake at 160°C fan for 20 to 25 minutes until the rhubarb is tender but still holding its shape. Check at 20 minutes, a thin piece of rhubarb should give easily when pressed with a spoon, and the colour should have shifted from bright pink to a softer, slightly translucent coral. Do not over-bake or the batons will collapse.

Remove from the oven and leave to cool in the dish, covered. Transfer to the fridge once at room temperature. To serve, lift the rhubarb batons carefully into shallow bowls and spoon the blush-pink syrup over. Serve with thick Greek yoghurt, crème fraîche, or whipped cream alongside.

items.symptom: The rhubarb has collapsed into mush
items.cause: Over-baked, or the pieces were too thin.
items.fix: Cut batons at least 1.5cm thick and check at 18 minutes. Remove as soon as they are just tender. Very thin rhubarb can be done in as little as 15 minutes.

items.cause: The rhubarb released a lot of liquid.
items.fix: Pour the syrup into a small pan and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes to reduce slightly. Pour back over the cooled rhubarb.

items.symptom: The rhubarb is still very tart
items.cause: Field rhubarb (main crop, late season) is sharper than forced rhubarb.
items.fix: Increase the sugar to 100g. Main-crop rhubarb in summer is noticeably sharper than the forced rhubarb available in January and February.

content.text: Keeps in the fridge, in its syrup, for up to 2 days. The rhubarb softens slightly further in storage. Do not freeze, it will turn mushy.
